meta.author: deep: O'Hare & Midway awards and capital tables
meta.description: Second pass on the FAA AIP carryover lines (awards with unspent money on the Aug 1 2025 carryover date not named in aviation.json), plus the O'Hare and Midway capital program tables as side facts on the airport bond lines. See research/aviation_awards.md.

pieces.name: Extend/expand taxiway (FAA grant 31700221962024)

source.doc: USASpending.gov award record and award funding history

pieces.why: The FAA promised this money to the City for one airport project. On the day the budget counted carryover the City had not yet been paid any of it, so the whole grant was waiting to be used.
pieces.note: Award 31700221962024 (Airport Improvement Program (entitlement or discretionary)): 29,481,263.00 awarded, period 2024-09-10 to 2028-09-09. The box is the unspent balance on 2025-08-01 (obligated minus gross outlays reported through July 2025), because that is the date the Budget Book uses to calculate carryover. Treasury has since reported gross outlays of 22,419,527.71 (through the latest report in the file), so little may be left to pay today. The first pass named only awards with money still unspent today, so this one was missing. FAA grant history lists it as 3-17-0022-196-2024.

residual.name: Still not tied to any FAA award, even on the carryover date
residual.why: The budget carries this much federal airport grant money over from earlier years. Federal records show awards with unspent money on the day the carryover was counted, but they explain only about a third of it. No public record ties the rest to a project.

splits.note: Second pass on this box. Unspent money on every named O'Hare FAA award on 2025-08-01 (the date the Budget Book says carryover is counted) adds up to $146,095,270, against the $411,790,000 carried. Awards made after that date, the IIJA 2026 awards, expired grants, and awards already named in the first pass are not repeated.
